scope: Native-composed managed Skill source removal with strict lineage checks and ordered source/projection history, including bounded install/remove/reinstall, recognized bundle upgrade, restart, backup/restore, retry and second-restore scenarios.
boundary: Exclusive native-owned disposable fixtures and bounded local tests only. No real Knowledge Root, production authority, workstream acceptance, full old-suite parity or cutover qualification is claimed.

sourceRemovalBoundary.scope: Remove only an existing managed lineage; preserve unrelated/custom sources.
sourceRemovalBoundary.input: Strict operationId UUID, sourceSha256, sourceManifestSHA, destSHA (nullable), and destManifestSHA (nullable with destSHA).
sourceRemovalBoundary.idempotency: Uses the same JSON fingerprint shape {actor,binding,input} and the global operation-id namespace; existing install fingerprints/history remain unchanged.
sourceRemovalBoundary.authority: Native approveRemovePlan and reconcileRemoveAnchor callbacks are both required and must be available; approvals and native authorization remain outside SQL.
sourceRemovalBoundary.history: Typed remove history uses kind 'remove'; old install history remains undiscriminated and unchanged. Ordered source/projection history is required; mixed source and older projection journals are denied.
sourceRemovalBoundary.unknownOutcomes: Unknown partial unlink, directory removal or post-commit anchor outcomes require exact native recovery. Startup never applies or guesses recovery.
sourceRemovalBoundary.platformHandling: Unix no-follow bounded UTF-8 handling is limited to disposable fixtures.

limitations: This is native-composed writer behavior in exclusive native-owned disposable fixtures, not a general installer/remover or production authority.
Only exact native source, target, owner, epoch, plan and anchor bindings authorize effects; operation arguments, hashes and HTTP/MCP callers do not create authority.
Mixed old projection/source journals remain denied because they cannot prove shared source-version ordering.
Unknown partial unlink, directory-removal and post-commit anchor outcomes require exact native recovery; no startup replay or guessed recovery is supported.
Unix no-follow bounded UTF-8 handling is fixture-bounded and does not establish hostile external-writer exclusion or an OS-level lock.

Backup/retry/restart flows are covered by the bounded functional command, but this is not Skill power-loss durability, full fault cross-product, full original parity, an accepted workstream, or cutover.
